why: Rule 1 at the only deg-3 junction: the 5.8 cm proton starts cool (70k) and rises to ~190k away from it, and the 12 cm heavy prong stops with a 375k spike at 10000, so every prong points away.
Rule 1 clean deg-3: two short proton stubs peaking at 220k and 240k rise away, plus the 20011+20013+20009 chain is one 128 cm muon with a textbook template Bragg reaching 245k at 20003.

Rule 1: both heavy prongs rise away from 59038 and terminate in real Bragg ends at 59037 and 59039, and the free end of the 131 cm MIP (11004) sits 5 cm away, so this is the fitted start of the hadronic prongs.

Only rule-1-consistent point in the event (the 116 cm muon cools toward it and a 2.7 cm stub hangs there), but it sits on the y=+200 top face so an entering cosmic is equally likely; the isolated 14 cm cluster 57 is the alternative.
Rule 1: the 42 cm proton rises monotonically along the brown template from 87k to 262k away from this junction, and the other prong is a 284 cm flat MIP muon exiting the bottom wall.

Deg-3 hadronic star with three short heavy prongs, the most upstream real structure in a compact downstream-corner event; alternative is 17002 with its 18 cm proton Bragg (267k) 24 cm further downstream.

Trap 3 kills the apparent rule-1 winner 11004 (170 deg pair and the zoom shows literally no kink), so the cluster is one 84 cm track; rule 3 puts the Michel-like 5 cm stub at 11003, making 11001 the start end.
Rule 1, 2 of 2 with real template Bragg peaks at both far ends: 108 cm muon rising to 215k at 7004 and 46 cm proton rising to 235k at 7003, with a 112 deg opening so trap 3 does not apply.

The only structure is an 8.6 cm proton whose dQ/dx falls monotonically along the proton template from 270k at 3000 to 78k here, so this is its cool start end; a 2.2 cm MIP stub 2.3 cm away supports a vertex.

In a 106-cluster mess I took the deg-4 knot that launches the 113.8 cm pi+ (stopping hot at 9000) and carries a 164k proton stub, but 9020 at 1.8 cm, shower apex 9007 and the hot star 9025 are all live alternatives.

Cluster 10 is an entering-top-face stopping cosmic, leaving only cluster 18, where 18011 is a localized 120-140k core with both prongs cooling away from it and prong B re-rising to 82k at 18015; 18014 6.6 cm upstream is the rule-1-clean rival.

Rule 1 plus rule 3 at a 124 deg elbow: the 80 cm muon rises along the template to 175k at 24001 with a Michel-like blip 7.6 cm past it, and the other prong is a 42 cm 1.5-2x MIP track exiting the z=500 face.

The event is twelve sub-centimetre blips at 11-19k except one 1.1 cm stub at 191k (4.4x MIP), and a proton-like deposit originates at a vertex, so I named that stub at its lower-z end (4024 vs 4000, 1.1 cm apart).

The 185 cm cluster is an entering-stopping muon (MIP at the x=-201 face, monotone Bragg to 250k at 13002) so 13000 is the only rule-1-clean candidate, but everything else in the event is sub-centimetre.

Deg-3 point where a 7.8 cm prong genuinely originates (28k at the junction rising to 80k where it stops), while the 158 cm MIP passes straight through it at 175.7 deg, which drops the tier per trap 3.
